title: **Language mode and named-pipe capture under the Windows sandbox** — under the [Windows ACL sandbox](../../sandbox/sandbox-windows-acl/README.md), read-only pwsh starts in ConstrainedLanguage because its temp write denial makes PowerShell's...

attrs.text: **Language mode and named-pipe capture under the Windows sandbox** — under the [Windows ACL sandbox](../../sandbox/sandbox-windows-acl/README.md), read-only pwsh starts in ConstrainedLanguage because its temp write denial makes PowerShell's AppLocker probe fail closed: `Add-Type`, non-core .NET statics (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors, and the mode cannot be lifted from inside. Workspace-write's private temp lets the probe complete, so it stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. Both confined modes deny named-pipe opens, so a piped-stdio spawn inside a confined command fails with EPERM. The tool description teaches both contracts to the model; the backend README owns the full limitations.

title: **Native ownership has explicit host requirements** — Linux needs a readable user manager whose `systemd-run` supports `--collect` (systemd 236 and later) and keeps scope arguments literal: version 254 and later receive `--expand-environmen...

attrs.text: **Native ownership has explicit host requirements** — Linux needs a readable user manager whose `systemd-run` supports `--collect` (systemd 236 and later) and keeps scope arguments literal: version 254 and later receive `--expand-environment=no`, and earlier versions, whose scope mode never expands arguments, run without it. Hosts without a usable user manager use the warned PGID fallback. macOS always uses that fallback because no supported public persistent owner exists.

title: **Native selection has bounded per-spawn costs** — Linux checks the bootstrap entry, libc `execve`/`fcntl` bindings, reachable user manager, and literal-argv scope probe on the first eligible ordinary or terminal spawn and keeps that verdic...

attrs.text: **Native selection has bounded per-spawn costs** — Linux checks the bootstrap entry, libc `execve`/`fcntl` bindings, reachable user manager, and literal-argv scope probe on the first eligible ordinary or terminal spawn and keeps that verdict, including a failed or timed-out probe. The user manager is identified by the process listening on `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/systemd/private`, the socket `systemd-run --user` connects through, as listed in the kernel's unix socket table (`/proc/net/unix`) for the same network namespace; reading the table costs time proportional to its size. After a positive verdict, each eligible spawn probes again when the `systemd-run` found through `PATH` has a different device, inode, size, or modification time, and otherwise confirms the manager: a listener confirms it without a child process; otherwise one `systemctl --user show` query decides, and that spawn uses the fallback when the query fails. A scope launch whose bootstrap never consumed its launch request, such as one sent to a hung manager that still listens, fails that command, as do scope launches issued before that failure arrives, and the next eligible spawn probes again. After a negative verdict, the provider probes again only when a different listener appears, so a manager that starts later is used without a restart. Windows rechecks the runner entry, bindings, and current Job support before every ordinary spawn. Fallback-warning de-duplication also persists for the provider lifetime. All prob...

title: **Windows Job inheritance has defined exclusions** — ordinary descendants inherit the Job by default, but breakaway processes are outside the guarantee. The target starts only after Job assignment; external termination of the runner in the ...

attrs.text: **Windows Job inheritance has defined exclusions** — ordinary descendants inherit the Job by default, but breakaway processes are outside the guarantee. The target starts only after Job assignment; external termination of the runner in the narrow create-to-assignment interval can leave a suspended target behind.

title: **Windows terminal signalling is console-wide** — SIGINT is delivered as a `\x03` Ctrl-C input write that the console host turns into a console-wide CTRL_C event (on Windows that host is node-pty's bundled OpenConsole); SIGTSTP and SIGHUP a...

attrs.text: **Windows terminal signalling is console-wide** — SIGINT is delivered as a `\x03` Ctrl-C input write that the console host turns into a console-wide CTRL_C event (on Windows that host is node-pty's bundled OpenConsole); SIGTSTP and SIGHUP are rejected as unavailable; a `taskkill` without `/F` does not terminate console processes, so the teardown TERM tier is a grace wait before the `/F` escalation. Windows readiness has no exact stdin-wait tier: the prompt-marker fast path compares the shell pid as the pseudo foreground group, and silence/timing tiers cover the rest.

title: **Windows terminal allocation requires node-pty's bundled console host assets** — every Windows terminal is spawned with `useConptyDll: true`, so allocation resolves `conpty/conpty.dll` and `OpenConsole.exe` relative to node-pty's own addon...

attrs.text: **Windows terminal allocation requires node-pty's bundled console host assets** — every Windows terminal is spawned with `useConptyDll: true`, so allocation resolves `conpty/conpty.dll` and `OpenConsole.exe` relative to node-pty's own addon; an asset that is missing or unpacked wrong makes `spawnTerminal` throw instead of falling back to the operating system console host. node-pty marks the option experimental, so a node-pty upgrade can change this behaviour. See the [bundled console host note](../../../.agents/notes/implemented/bug-fix/2026-09-28-pty-bundled-console-host.md).

attrs.text: **Fallback terminal ownership remains observational** — on macOS or Linux without usable user-systemd, a child that reparents before any foreground-inspection snapshot or leaves the owned terminal session can escape the process-table scan. The local provider does not add a continuous process-table monitor; supported Linux native mode instead retains these descendants through scope membership.

title: **In-process cleanup requires a JavaScript-observable exit** — direct `process.exit()`, default uncaught exceptions, and default unhandled rejections emit Node's synchronous `exit` event. The default OS disposition for an unhandled `SIGTERM...

attrs.text: **In-process cleanup requires a JavaScript-observable exit** — direct `process.exit()`, default uncaught exceptions, and default unhandled rejections emit Node's synchronous `exit` event. The default OS disposition for an unhandled `SIGTERM`, `SIGINT`, or `SIGHUP` bypasses that event; an application covers those signals only by installing a handler that performs normal disposal or calls `process.exit()`. `SIGKILL`, fatal OOM, `process.abort()`, native crashes, power loss, and any failure that cannot run JavaScript require an external supervisor, container init, or equivalent OS owner.

attrs.text: **Create-to-assignment interruption** — the target starts suspended and cannot execute before Job assignment, but an external termination of the runner in the narrow interval between process creation and assignment can leave the suspended target behind. The package does not claim atomic Job attachment.

attrs.text: **pwsh bootstrap in a constrained sandbox** — the prompt function and UTF-8 pin write through `[Console]::`, which the Windows ACL sandbox's read-only mode may deny. When that prevents marker readiness, startup rejects at `timeoutMs` instead of publishing an incomplete shell.
